newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Chirac thanks ex-UN chief Boutros-Ghali.
newsitem.headline: France's Chirac thanks ex-UN chief Boutros-Ghali.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac, who battled Washington in vain for the reappointment of Boutros Boutros-Ghali as U.N. secretary-general, warmly thanked the Egyptian on Friday for his five years leading the world body.

During a meeting of nearly an hour at the presidential palace, Chirac "spoke of his esteem for (Boutros-Ghali) and thanked him again for all he had done as secretary-general," presidential spokeswoman Catherine Colonna said.
Boutros-Ghali, who left the U.N. leadership on December 31, aged 74, and was succeeded by Ghanaian Kofi Annan, in turn thanked Chirac for his support, Colonna said.

Boutros-Ghali, a former Egyptian official and law professor who speaks fluent French, was barred from a second term by a U.S. veto despite strong support for his reappointment from Paris and virtually every other world capital.
Washington said it wanted a more reform-minded leader, but most U.N. diplomats blamed U.S. political considerations during a presidential election year for his demise.
